demand_obligation_certainty.note: Regulation (EU) 2025/2365 is adopted and published (not a proposal) — multi-source convergence via WebSearch aggregation. High but not 1.0: this session could not independently re-read the primary EUR-Lex text to rule out an error in the secondary-source convergence. See evidence pack section 1.

demand_suppression_risk.note: Mechanism is real and evidenced: EMAS-registered operators are exempt from third-party certification if their EMAS verifier verifies compliance instead; operators below the 1500 t/year certification threshold (including all micro-enterprises) may use self-declaration instead of third-party certification. Both remove demand for a NEW certifier's services. Magnitude (what fraction of in-scope operators these routes cover) was not found. See evidence pack section 3.

shock_date_stability.note: No source found assessing amendment/delay risk for the 2027-12-17 date specifically, in either direction. Absence of evidence of instability is not evidence of stability — left INSUFFICIENT_DATA rather than assumed favorable. See evidence pack section 2.

record.summary: Regulation (EU) 2025/2365 on preventing plastic pellet losses requires large/medium operators handling >=1500 t/year to hold third-party certification of compliance by 2027-12-17, issued by a certification body accredited (ISO/IEC 17065 and/or 17021, plastics-sector scope) under the OCS Europe scheme. Candidate question: is there a de-novo-entrant calendar arbitrage opportunity in becoming such an accredited certifier before the deadline. See real-case-001-evidence-pack.md for full sourcing, caveats, and the access-constraint note (direct WebFetch to EUR-Lex/Consilium/EC was blocked this session; facts below are WebSearch-aggregated and flagged accordingly).
